function: Learned RIS partitioning (cascaded DNNs) and DDPG-based active beamforming, passive RIS phase shifts and NOMA power allocation, maximizing sum rate; K-GMM clusters users (p. 3, p. 7-9).
system: mmWave NOMA downlink at 28 GHz: BS with N=32 ULA antennas, K single-antenna users, reflecting RIS with M=128 UPA elements, 3-bit phases, no direct link (p. 3-4, p. 10).
method: Cascaded DNN pair trained label-free on sum-rate loss for RIS partitioning; DDPG actor-critic reinforcement learning for beamforming and power; K-means plus GMM user clustering (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels, 7 paths, 28 GHz, path-loss parameters from [5], Gaussian CSI error; no standard model or dataset (p. 4-5, p. 10).
test_conditions: One simulated scenario (users in a 10 m circle); sweeps over Pmax, REs, users; training-execution mismatch only discussed as future work, no test (p. 9-13).
baselines: Non-learned: AO (S3), zero-forcing with random RIS phases (S2), no RIS (S1); learned: Q-learning, DQN, DDQN, supervised partitioning of [25] (S4); clustering: K-means, GMM; partitioning: none, average (p. 10-13).
metrics: Sum achievable rate in bps/Hz versus iterations, transmit power, number of REs and users; beam patterns (p. 10-14).
complexity: none; only qualitative remarks on lower computational overhead (p. 3, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "We utilize the Saleh-Valenzuela model [31] to represent the mmWave channel for both the BS-RIS and RIS-User links"; path-loss parameters from [5] (p. 10). Custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data; missing.
q2_support: p. 9: "The performance of DRL algorithms may be degraded if the training environment is significantly different from the actual execution environment" (Remark 1, left to future research); Figs. 4-11 (p. 11-14) sweep power, REs and users, but no passage says a trained model is tested on a condition unseen in training; missing.
q3_support: p. 12: "we compare the proposed method with the following three DRL models, namely Q-learning [37], Deep Q-Network (DQN) [38], and Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) [39]"; p. 13: "AO-based RIS-assisted mmWave-NOMA system (denoted as S3)" and S4, the supervised partitioning of [25]; comparisons are on the sum achievable rate (Figs. 7-11).
q4_support: p. 3: "They can solve non-convex optimization problems with minimal computational complexity through feature learning and model training" is qualitative; iteration counts to convergence (p. 10) are not a cost; no complexity order, operations, parameters or runtime anywhere; missing.
q5_support: p. 10: "Assuming the number of paths for channel modeling is 7 and the operating frequency is 28 GHz" (own simulated channels); no link to code or data and no public dataset; the channel knowledge map is only future work (p. 9, p. 14); missing.
notes: Area 3: the learned elements are the RIS partitioning DNNs and the DDPG agent for beamforming, RIS phases and power in a RIS-assisted NOMA downlink; K-GMM user clustering is classical clustering. System check passes: BS has 32 antennas and a RIS (p. 3). q3: DQN, DDQN, Q-learning and the supervised partitioning of [25] are learned baselines; AO (S3) and zero-forcing with random RIS phases (S2) are non-learned. q1: Saleh-Valenzuela is a textbook model, so not counted.
